raw_response:
I'll reason through this as the farmer first, then give the structured plan.

---

I've been working this land for forty years. My father showed me, his father showed him. I can't read, but I know what my fields do. Forty-two mu is a fair bit — me and the missus can't do it all alone, but our two grown kids help on weekends and the old mother watches the little one. Five mouths at home means I can't have a bad year.

Let me walk through what I'm doing this year, field by field.

**The wheat-maize land — about 28 mu of it.** This is the bread and butter. I planted the wheat back in early October like always, the day after the old Li family down the road. I put down one bag of diammonium (二铵) per mu before I plowed — that's what I've always done, one bag per mu, nothing fancy. When the spring comes and the wheat starts jointing, I'll spread about half a bag of urea per mu on top. If the wheat looks yellow I might add a bit more. I already watered it once before the ground froze, and I'll water it maybe three more times — once after the spring green-up, once at jointing when I topdress, and once when the grain is filling. Water costs money at the well, but wheat won't give you anything without water here. Last year I got about 450 kg per mu, which is what I usually get. Nothing special.

Soon as the wheat comes off in early June, I got maybe five days to get the maize in. No time to plow. I've got a neighbor with a no-till planter — I give him some money and he runs it through for me. Hybrid maize seed, whatever the shop in town has that everyone's using this year — Zhengdan or Xianyu, one of those. I put one bag of compound fertilizer (复合肥) down with the planter, and when the maize is about knee-high I'll spread urea, maybe half a bag per mu. If it rains good I don't water at all. If July is dry I'll water once. Maize usually gives me 500 kg, sometimes more if the summer rains come right.

**The cotton — 10 mu on the sandier piece to the west.** Cotton is more trouble than grain but the price is better if you get a good pick. I plant it late April when the ground is warm enough. I use one bag of compound at planting. Cotton gets bugs — I spray maybe four or five times through the summer, whatever the shop tells me to use against the aphids and the bollworm. I water it maybe twice if no rain comes. My wife and daughter-in-law do most of the picking in September and October, hand-picking, several rounds. I get maybe 250 kg of lint per mu in a normal year.

**The cucumber — 4 mu next to the house.** This is the cash. I grow open-field cucumber for the summer market in town. My wife mostly manages this — she knows more about vegetables than I do. We put a lot of fertilizer on it, maybe four bags of compound per mu over the season plus manure from the neighbor's chicken place. Water it every few days from the well. Sprays for downy mildew. Lots of labor — staking, tying, picking every other day from July through September. It's tiring but the cash helps us through winter.

I'm not trying anything new this year. What worked last year will work this year. I keep some cash reserve in case the pump breaks down or somebody gets sick.
